title: Adversarial Attack and Defense for Denoising Diffusion Sampling
claim: A sequential sampling chain is exposed to adversarial perturbation at one step and protected by a regularized defense at the next.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right chain of variables, red attack arrow above, blue defense arrow below
description: A single horizontal chain of mathematical variables joined by black arrows, read left to right. It starts at x_k, then goes to the perturbed x̃_k, then to the Monte Carlo samples z̃_{k,i}, then to the score estimate s̃(t_k, x̃_k), and ends at x_{k+1}. The last two arrows are labeled in italics: 'Score Estimation' and 'Backward Process'. A red label above the first arrow reads 'Inject Adversarial Perturbation δ_{k-1}', with a red arrow pointing down onto the x_k→x̃_k step. A blue label below reads 'Defend with Local Variation Regularized V', with a blue arrow pointing up into the x̃_k→z̃ step. The red and blue colors make the attack and defense points stand out. The bottom blue text is slightly cropped. The white background keeps it minimal.
caption: Diagram of the entire adversarial attack and defense scheme for denoising diffusion sampling in a decentralized scenario. While variable xk (the simplified version of xtk) is transmitted from the (k −1)-th user to the k-th user, an adversarial perturbation δk−1 can be injected to yield a perturbed variable ˜xk. In the defense side, the local variation regularized V • not only tolerates adversarial perturbations, but also integrates with a zeroth-order rejection sampling scheme to produce MC samples ˜zt,i. Then the score estimation and backward process can be implemented to produce the next variable xk+1. In the next round, xk+1 may still be attacked and the same attack-defense dynamic continues.
abstract: Denoising diffusion sampling (DDS) is an emerging approach for generating new samples that have the same distribution as some training samples. However, it is vulnerable to adversarial attacks by even a Gaussian perturbation. In this work, we propose a complete set of adversarial attack and defense methodology for DDS. In the attack side, we propose to inject a perturbation to the sampling stage, which significantly worsen the performance of sample generation. In the defense side, we propose a local variation based regularization model for the potential function minimization, which effectively tolerates the adversarial perturbations. Moreover, we develop a conjugate gradient algorithm to solve the defense model, which integrates with a recently-developed zeroth order rejection sampling method that saves computational cost. Experimental results show that the proposed attack significantly worsen the existing state-of-the-art methods, but can be defended by the proposed local variation regularization.
